chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb Al-Mithammi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem for the performer of Tamattu' if he does not enter into Ihram from the night of Tarwiyah, whenever it is easy for him, as long as he does not fear missing the two stations.

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: The two stations (referring to Arafat and Muzdalifah)
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The night of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.لِلْمُتَمَتِّعِ: For the performer of Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim performing Tamattu' enter Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of Hajj al-Tamattu' is not compromised by delaying the Ihram ritual until the night of Tarwiyah, as long as the pilgrim can manage the transition without risking the missed opportunity of the two critical stations (Arafat and Muzdalifah). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (yusr) and the preservation of the core pillars of Hajj over rigid adherence to specific timings for the preliminary state of consecration.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb Al Maysami who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘There is no problem for the performer of Tumatto if he does not wear Ihraam from the night of Tarwiyya (8th Zil Hijjaj) whenever it is easy for him for as long as he does not fear losing the two pausing stations’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb al-Mithamiy who has said the following: “

I heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘It is not harmful to one who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) to assume the state of Ihram in the night of al-Tarwiyah (eight of Dhu al-Hajj ah) whenever possible for him, as long as he is not afraid of losing the two al-Mawqafan (stations, Mina’ and ‘Arafat).”’
